findings.source_passage: "Queequeg," said I, when they had dragged me, the last man, to the deck, and I was still shaking myself in my jacket to fling off the water
findings.source_locator: paragraph 2, opening of the dialogue sequence
findings.why_it_matters: The detail of being 'dragged' 'the last man' to the deck is narratively specific and characterizes Ishmael's hapless, last-rescued position; the draft's 'shaking off the water' loses this comic-pathetic image entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'dragged me, the last man, to the deck' in the Queequeg exchange to preserve the mock-heroic self-deprecation.

findings.source_passage: the particular disaster to our own particular boat was chiefly to be imputed to Starbuck's driving on to his whale almost in the teeth of a squall, and considering that Starbuck, notwithstanding, was famous for his great heedfulness
findings.why_it_matters: The long anaphoric 'considering … considering … considering' chain is a signature rhetorical device of this chapter—its cumulative irony is central to how Melville builds Ishmael's mock-legal reasoning. The draft collapses it into a single compressed clause, losing the prosodic and satirical effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least three 'considering' clauses with their parallel structure to preserve the satirical legal-rhetoric set piece.

summary: The draft preserves all verbatim signature passages faithfully, with only two medium-level voice flattenings in the dialogue attribution and the anaphoric 'considering' chain that do not individually rise to regeneration threshold.
